newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK SHARES EASE IN THIN PRE-HOLIDAY TRADE.
newsitem.headline: TURK SHARES EASE IN THIN PRE-HOLIDAY TRADE.

text.p: Istanbul shares dropped in subdued trade on Wednesday ahead of a 6-1/2-day holiday beginning from mid-Thurday, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed down 12 points, or 0.78 percent at 1,523 after moving between 1,514 and 1,547. Trade volume retreated to 14.07 trillion lira from Tuesday's 17.52 trillion.
"Volume was very low and trade margins were narrow due to the approaching holiday. Only a few stocks were active. I expect this trend to continue tomorrow," said Fatih Aslanoba from Alfa securities.
The market will close after the first session on Thursday and reopen on April 24, Thursday, due to a 4-1/2-day religious holiday to be followed by a national holiday on April 23.
"I expect some selling next Thursday and Friday ahead of the National Security Council (MGK) meeting," Aslanoba said.

The market is unnerved by the MGK meeting scheduled for April 26 following a rift which emerged between the coalition's Islamist and conservative wings after the secularist military demanded measures against rising Islamist zeal in the February 28 MGK meeting.

Delay in settlements of share transactions because of the holiday had produced a 2.2 percent rise on Tuesday. Brokers said players who bought yesterday were on the selling side today so as not to carry share positions over the long holiday.
Deals done yesterday will be settled on April 24 and those made today and on Thursday morning will be settled on April 25.
Investors switching to cash or repo deals ahead of the holiday had caused volume to shrink last week and on Monday.

Of the 247 shares traded, falls outdid rises by 108 to 76 and 63 were stable. The IMKB Industrial shed 0.52 percent to 1,525, the IMKB Services lost 1.18 percent to 1,426 and the IMKB Financial eased 0.49 percent to 1,636.

Top actives were commercial vehicle venture Anadolu Isuzu, down 1,000 lira at 79,000, utility Cukurova Elektrik, down 5,000 lira at 200,000 and T. Isbank's C series shares, up 500 lira at 45,000. They made up 18.5 percent of the total turnover.
